unmapped_findings: For the present condition (1150 °C, 10 s⁻¹) the Fe-Mn-Al-C steel is a negative temperature-sensitive and positive strain-rate-sensitive material: flow (rheological) stress increases with increasing strain rate or decreasing temperature, so peak stress can be reduced by decreasing ε̇ or increasing T (b0012, b0021, b0024, b0084).

High-strain-rate trend relevant to this sample: at the high strain rate 10 s⁻¹ the peak stress decreases by 73% within the 900–1150 °C range (for comparison, at 0.01 s⁻¹ it decreases from 305.4 MPa at 900 °C to 53.8 MPa at 1150 °C, an 82% reduction). These are range statements for the 10 s⁻¹ series, not a discrete value for 1150 °C/10 s⁻¹ (b0024).
This sample's lnZ (Table 1, 10 s⁻¹ column, 1150 °C row) = 58.92, the lowest lnZ among the reported conditions; lnZ increases with increasing strain rate and decreasing temperature (table_001, b0037).
The 1150 °C/10 s⁻¹ condition lies outside the fine-and-uniform-grain hot-working windows recommended by the authors: 950–1000 °C/0.01–0.1 s⁻¹ and 1050–1100 °C/1–10 s⁻¹ (b0012, b0065, b0086).

No optical micrograph is provided for exactly 1150 °C/10 s⁻¹; Fig. 9 covers 1150 °C only at 1 s⁻¹ (panel f) and 10 s⁻¹ only at 1100 °C (panel c), so the deformed microstructure of this exact sample is only represented through its measured DRX average grain size (~20–25 µm, figure_010/figure_011).

For context (other condition, not this sample): at 1150 °C and 0.01 s⁻¹ the DRX grain size exceeds 70 µm and the structure is coarse-grained, indicating rapid recrystallized-grain growth (b0063, figure_010).

As-forged initial microstructure of the steel shows pronounced banded segregation contrast (fine parallel striations within every grain), i.e. chemical heterogeneity in the as-forged condition (figure_001).

Material-level hot-deformation constants derived from the full experimental matrix (not this single condition): DRX activation energy Qp = 669.844 kJ mol⁻¹; R = 8.314 J/(mol·K); α = 0.00599; k1 = 5.135; k2 = 15.690; C = 0.1461 at 1050 °C/0.01 s⁻¹ (R = 0.9728); εc/εp ≈ 0.452 (b0029, b0032, b0045, b0054, figure_005).
The steel composition (mass fraction, %) is 1.46 C, 25.14 Mn, 10 Al, 0.053 Nb, balance Fe, i.e. the alloy of this sample (b0018).

The experiments were confirmed to be reproducible: isothermal constant-strain-rate compression tests on the same steel batch/composition under identical conditions were used to check the reproducibility of the proposed system, and the reported experimental phenomena have reproducibility (b0018, b0024, b0037, b0058, b0065).
